Possibly they mean "I want to confirm that the seamless pants do not have three seams" or "I want to confirm that the seamless pants don't have three holes"? They might be asking about a product detail: "celana seamless" means seamless pants. "nga ada tiga2" maybe "doesn't have three [holes]"? Or "doesn't have three [something]"? Could be "tiga-tiga" meaning "three times"? Hard to parse.

They might be asking to confirm that the seamless pants do not have three seams. So we need to respond confirming that the seamless pants indeed do not have three seams. But we also need to ask clarifying question: "Could you clarify what you mean by 'tiga2'?" We should ask them to clarify what they refer to as "tiga2".
